pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Anti-NMDA Receptor Encephalitis (Paraneoplastic Etiology) THE SMOKING GUN: A targeted pelvic transvaginal ultrasound and MRI revealing a 4.2 cm mature cystic ovarian teratoma (dermoid cyst) containing ectopic neural elements. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: The patient's ovarian teratoma contained ectopic neural tissue expressing GluN1 subunits of the N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor. The immune system recognized these tissue elements as foreign, mounting an antibody response. Pathogenic IgG antibodies crossed the blood-brain barrier and bound to extracellular epitopes of the GluN1 subunit of neuronal NMDA receptors in the hippocampus and forebrain. This antibody binding induced cross-linking and internalisation of the receptors, resulting in a state of severe cerebral NMDA receptor hypofunction without causing cellular death. The loss of NMDA receptor function disrupts GABAergic inhibition, triggering uninhibited dopaminergic and glutamate signaling—manifesting sequentially as psychosis, catatonia, choreoathetoid dyskinesias, autonomic instability, and central hypoventilation. Emergency surgical resection of the teratoma followed by high-dose corticosteroids, intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG), and plasma exchange leads to full neurological recovery over months.
